findings.title: Readiness probe misclassifies git timeouts/failures as NOT_A_CHECKOUT or DETACHED_HEAD
findings.description: Description: Both probe catches treat *any* `gitExec` rejection as the specific signal they are probing. `checkoutReadiness` passes `FIX_GIT_TIMEOUT_MS` to these calls, and the constant's own docstring says the bound exists "to cover a hanging hook or a stuck lock". When a read-only probe hits that bound (e.g. a stuck network filesystem, or any unexpected git failure), `rev-parse --show-toplevel` timing out is reported to the user as `NOT_A_CHECKOUT` ("checkout missing or not a git checkout") and `symbolic-ref -q HEAD` timing out as `DETACHED_HEAD` ("checkout is on a detached HEAD") — a wrong cause for exactly the failure mode the timeout was added for, violating the project rule to fail explicitly rather than substitute a misleading value. The behavior is still safe (the fix is deferred, nothing is written), and neither case has a test, so the misclassification is invisible in CI. Suggested fix: inspect the error (e.g. `gitExec`'s timeout message) and either rethrow, or block with a reason that says "probe failed" rather than asserting the checkout is missing/detached; add a test that stubs a rejecting `gitExec` to pin the label.

findings.title: A failure mid-apply leaves earlier checkouts written/committed with only a raw error
findings.description: Description: `applyFixPlan` (packages/core/src/introspection/routedFixes.ts, `applyFixPlan`/`applyPlanEntry`) applies plan entries sequentially with no per-entry fault isolation. If an unexpected error escapes one entry (the apply-time `gateByReadiness` re-probe can throw on a git timeout, unlike plan time where the same call is inside the same probe — same risk, but plan time happens before any writes), the whole call rejects: entries already applied are committed in their checkouts and the invoking checkout's writes stay uncommitted, and the user sees only the raw git error from `handleError`/`errorResult` with no indication that an earlier checkout was already fixed. The state is recoverable (re-running checks finds only the remaining findings), so this is informational, but a brief "applied in N checkout(s) before stopping" note on the error path would make partial application explicit.

findings.title: `fixAction!` non-null assertions rely on an upstream filter invariant
findings.description: Description: `fixRelPath` (packages/core/src/introspection/routedFixes.ts:59) and `routeView`'s use of `finding.fixAction!.subjectIndex` (line 143) force-unwrap `fixAction`. Every current call site guards with `fixable && fixAction` first (see `planRoutedFixes`' `fixableOf` and `applyFixes`), so this is safe today, but the type contract of `ConsistencyFinding` allows `fixable: true` with `fixAction` undefined, so a future rule emitting an unguarded fixable finding would crash `planRoutedFixes` instead of degrading to a deferral. A one-line comment on `fixRelPath` naming the invariant, or a guard that defers with `OWNER_UNRESOLVED`/skips, would make the contract local to this module.

findings.title: Multi-checkout fix output prints each applied fix's detail twice
findings.description: Description: In multi-checkout fix mode, `printCheckOutput` first renders every finding with its matched `→ Fixed: before → after in <path>` line (checkReport.ts:88-90, via `formatFinding`), then the `fixRes && showWorktree` branch (line 95) calls `printRoutedFixResult`, which re-prints the same before/after lines grouped by checkout (packages/cli/src/output/fixReport.ts, `printRoutedFixResult`). For the invoking checkout's and each committed checkout's writes the user sees the change detail twice in one run. The existing grouping test (packages/cli/tests/commands/check-worktree-fix.test.ts, "groups the invoking write...") only asserts the grouped section, so the duplication isn't pinned either way — worth a deliberate decision (e.g. suppress the per-finding `Fixed:` line when `showWorktree` is true, since the grouped section carries it).

findings.title: Routing, committing, restoring, and deferral behavior is pinned by real-git tests
findings.description: Description: The test additions follow the house testing rules well: tests accompany the implementation across every tier (unit: `fixOwnership.test.ts`, `checkoutReadiness.test.ts`, `commitPaths.test.ts`; integration: `routedFixes.test.ts`, `subjectIndex` coverage; CLI/MCP end-to-end: `check-worktree-fix.test.ts`, `workflowCheckRouting.test.ts`). The shared `gitWorktreeFixture` helper uses real git with per-repo pinned identity, `commit.gpgsign=false`, and `core.hooksPath` so global config can't change outcomes; the rejecting-hook and restore-failure cases (routedFixes.test.ts cases 5–7) verify the D5a rollback contract against real git state (`porcelain`, `commitCount`, `lastSubject`). The `DEFER_REASON_LABELS` exhaustiveness test pins the label map to the `DeferReason` union, and the single-checkout cases assert no git process is spawned (`execFile` spy) — matching the SC 9 contract. No test reads any production/external environment variable, and fixtures are self-contained temp directories cleaned up in `afterEach`.
